record.paper_title: Methods for Computing All Roots of a Polynomial Simultaneously - Known Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Divergence conditions for the Weierstrass method
record.original_question: For the Weierstrass method that simultaneously approximates all roots of a monic polynomial f(x) of degree n, find sufficient conditions on the starting vector of distinct initial approximations x_i^0, i = 1, 2, ..., n, that force the iteration to diverge, and characterize the set of starting approximations satisfying those divergence conditions.

evidence.quote: Find sufficient conditions for the divergence of the Weierstrass method and describe the set of starting approximations x?, i = 1,2, ... ,n, satisfying these conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f(x) = x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + ... + a_0 be a monic polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 with complex coefficients, and let ξ_1, ..., ξ_n denote its (not necessarily distinct) zeros. The Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner) iteration is the map W : (ℂ \ Δ)^n → ℂ^n defined componentwise by

  W_i(x_1, ..., x_n) = x_i − f(x_i) / ∏_{j ≠ i} (x_i − x_j),  i = 1, ..., n,

where Δ denotes the diagonal {x : x_i = x_j for some i ≠ j}. Given a starting vector x^{(0)} = (x_1^{(0)}, ..., x_n^{(0)}) ∈ ℂ^n with pairwise distinct entries, the iteration is x^{(k+1)} = W(x^{(k)}) for k ≥ 0.

Problem: Provide sufficient conditions on the starting vector x^{(0)} (formulated in terms of f and the entries x_i^{(0)}) under which the Weierstrass iteration diverges, in the sense that the sequence {x^{(k)}} does not converge to any permutation of (ξ_1, ..., ξ_n) (allowing, e.g., that some component escapes to infinity, or that the sequence is attracted to a periodic orbit disjoint from the root set, or that a collision x_i^{(k)} = x_j^{(k)} occurs). Furthermore, describe (topologically and/or measure-theoretically) the set of all such starting vectors in ℂ^n that satisfy the proposed divergence conditions.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist. It is known that the Weierstrass–Durand–Kerner method is not generally convergent: for every degree d ≥ 3 there are open sets of polynomials whose Weierstrass dynamics admit attracting periodic orbits (Reinke–Schleicher–Stoll and others). Some specific divergence sets have been described (e.g., cycles for cubics, two-sided SOR variants), but a complete characterization of sufficient divergence conditions and the resulting set of starting approximations remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Weierstrass-Durand-Kerner root finder is not generally convergent
status_evidence.snippet: There are open sets of polynomials of every degree d ≥ 3 such that the dynamics of the Weierstrass method applied to such polynomials exhibits attracting periodic orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Non-convergence of Weierstrass method is established for open sets of polynomials, but a full divergence characterization is not given.

status_evidence.title: On the divergent properties of two-sided SOR Weierstrass method
status_evidence.snippet: Divergent sets consist of an infinite number of divergent starting vectors but have measure zero for the methods considered.
status_evidence.claim: Partial descriptions of divergent starting-vector sets exist for SOR variants.

status_evidence.title: Convergence of the Weierstrass Method for Simultaneous Approximation of Polynomial Zeros
status_evidence.snippet: New semilocal results provide weaker sufficient convergence conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues on convergence/divergence conditions for Weierstrass method.
